## The question

> Are Cloudflare and Docker the same kind of thing?

**The walkaway:**

> Different jobs: Docker packs the app, Cloudflare delivers and protects the traffic.

## Script

| # | In | Type | s | Narration | Caption text (board) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0:00.0 | hook | 3.4 | Cloudflare and Docker both show up in web projects. | Two names, two jobs |
| 2 | 0:03.4 | analogy | 5.4 | Treating them as alternatives is like comparing a road network with a shipping box. | Not alternatives |
| 3 | 0:09.8 | explain | 4.7 | Docker packs an app with the pieces it needs: code, libraries, settings. | Packed with its pieces |
| 4 | 0:14.5 | explain | 4.4 | That package is an image. Run it, and it becomes a container. | Image, then container |
| 5 | 0:18.9 | explain | 4.4 | Cloudflare does a different job: it sits in front of your site. | In front of your site |
| 6 | 0:22.3 | step-by-step | 5.4 | It can route visitors, keep copies of pages near them, and block bad traffic. | Route, cache, shield |
| 7 | 0:28.7 | step-by-step | 6.4 | A team builds the app in Docker, runs it on a server, and puts Cloudflare in front. | Pack, run, front it |
| 8 | 0:34.1 | explain | 4.2 | Two layers, two jobs. The app is packed, the traffic is handled. | Two layers |
| 9 | 0:38.3 | compare | 4.7 | They are not competitors. Each does what the other does not. | Not competitors |
| 10 | 0:43.0 | myth-check | 4.4 | Cloudflare doesn't host your app. Docker doesn't secure it. | Neither one is automatic |
| 11 | 0:47.4 | recap | 3.4 | Docker packages the app. Cloudflare delivers and protects it. | Pack, deliver, protect |
| 12 | 0:51.8 | outro | 3.2 | Different jobs. Sometimes, one stack. | CLOUDFLARE vs DOCKER |
